title: ClipSAT Course Schema (v2 — blocks model)
description: This top-level shape (a whole course: id + meta + chapters[]) is documentation/illustration ONLY — see the 'examples' block below for a full worked case. What's actually validated file-by-file (scripts/validate-content.js) is #/definitions/courseMeta against content/{track}/_meta.json, and #/definitions/chapter against each content/{track}/{chapter-slug}.json — one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so editing one chapter never requires touching or re-reading a file with every other chapter in it. NOT the format bank-data/*.json question banks use — those have their own ad hoc shape and are intentionally left alone. v2 replaces the original fixed definitions/theorems/keyFormulas/workedExamples split (v1, never adopted) with an ordered blocks[] model, after v1 was found not to match real chapter markup during the WP6 qudrat pilot — see docs/DECISIONS/0002-blocks-model-not-fixed-fields.md.

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the filename, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

chapters.description: Ordered list of chapters (topics) in this course.

practiceSet.description: Validates content/{track}/_practice-set.json — the track's numbered free-response practice list (the 'Practice set' section, distinct from bank-data/*.json's MCQ pools and from chapter content). NOT a blocks[]-shaped chapter: this is a flat, repeated list of {number, question, solution, difficulty} items, which is what the real markup actually is (50 uniform <div class="problem"> items, verified converting qudrat, WP6). Optional per track — most tracks don't have this section yet.

courseMeta.description: Validates content/{track}/_meta.json — course-level metadata, kept separate from chapter files (one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so no single file needs the whole course read to edit one chapter).

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the track slug, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

chapterOrder.description: Ordered list of chapter ids, e.g. ['qud-about', 'qud-arithmetic', ...]. The filesystem's directory listing order is NOT reliable display order — this is the explicit source of truth both the nav rail and the page's chapter sequence render from. Every id here must have a matching content/{track}/{id}.json file; scripts/validate-content.js checks this.

meta.description: Top-level course metadata displayed on the home card and course header.

title.description: Human-readable course title, e.g. 'Digital SAT Math'.

subtitle.description: Short tagline shown below the title.

prerequisites.description: List of course IDs that are recommended before this course.

color.description: Brand accent colour (hex or CSS variable) — see docs/DESIGN_TOKENS.md, prefer a var(--token).

icon.description: Optional emoji or short string used on the card badge.

estimatedHours.description: Approximate study hours for the full course.

examBoard.description: Awarding body, e.g. 'College Board', 'IB', 'Cambridge'. Proper noun, not translated.

officialLinks.description: External links to the exam board's own official portal/past-papers pages, shown on the track's Downloads section (downloads-block.njk). Track-specific real data — e.g. qudrat links to Qiyas and ETEC.

downloadsInfo.description: The two small numbers downloads-block.njk's boilerplate copy needs per track (chapter count for the 'Print/Save as PDF' packet description, worksheet count for the Worksheet Library description below it — the worksheet grid itself is a live widget, public/js/engine.js populates <div class="worksheet-library" data-track>, not authored here).

pageHeader.description: The <section class="subject-head"> at the top of the track page — page <h1> + a small stat row. Distinct from meta.title (used in <title>/nav/cards) since the on-page H1 can read differently.

testGenerator.description: Config for test-generator.njk's 'Full official exam paper' button — genFullExam(title, trackId, sections[], minutes) is existing engine.js JS, this just supplies its real per-track arguments instead of hardcoding them in the template.

examTitle.description: Not translated — passed as a literal JS string argument.

sections.description: Not translated — passed as literal JS string arguments.

questionCount.description: Separate from minutes — don't assume they're equal even though they coincide for qudrat's real 52-question/52-minute exam.

bilingualText.description: Every user-facing string in this schema uses this shape. 'ar': null means not yet translated — render English only, no Arabic toggle for this string. dir="rtl" is derived from the active language at render time, never stored here. HTML/LaTeX allowed inside (matches source markup — e.g. inline \( ... \) math, /, and occasional embedded ... for an Arabic term inside otherwise-English prose).

id.description: Unique slug within the course, e.g. 'qud-about'.

chapterNumber.description: The short badge shown next to the chapter title AND in the nav rail (source: <span class="cn">), e.g. 'i', '1', '5'. A string, not an int — some tracks use non-numeric badges.

railLabel.description: Optional — the nav rail's label for this chapter, if it differs from `title` (real source cases exist where the rail link has an Arabic translation but the chapter's own <h2> doesn't, or vice versa — don't assume they match, check both). Falls back to `title` if absent.

description.description: Optional one-line summary/tag line shown under the title.

quizWidget.description: NOT quiz question data — every chapter's 'Chapter Quiz' section is a live widget (count/level selectors + a Generate button, genChapterQuiz() in engine.js) that pulls from bank-data/{track}.json at request time. This just tells the template whether to render that widget for this chapter.

chapterContent.description: All instructional material for a chapter, as an ORDERED sequence of blocks — order matters and is preserved from the source (unlike a v1-style split into separate definitions[]/theorems[]/etc. arrays, which loses document flow).

videos.description: Embedded topic videos (Appendix A benchmark task 6 — see docs/RECIPES.md #6).

provider.description: Extend this enum if a second provider is ever needed — don't add a differently-shaped field.

videoId.description: The provider's video ID (e.g. YouTube's 11-char ID), not a full URL.

topicTag.description: Optional free-text tag linking this video to a specific block by id.

block.description: A discriminated union on 'kind'. Kinds were derived from what real chapter markup actually contains (grep counts across index.html as of WP6, docs/DECISIONS/0002): 'callout' covers definition/theorem/note/warning/proof/worked-example boxes (489+398 real instances — they all share one label+body shape, differing only in a style class), 'table' (22 instances, e.g. an exam section map), 'cards' (212 instances, e.g. a Format/Calculator/Skills/Signature stat grid), 'text' for a plain paragraph with no wrapper, and 'explorer' (docs/DECISIONS/0003-explorer-block.md) for an interactive canvas widget — checked against 3 real instances (qudrat's qud-ratio ×2, qud-compare ×1), not guessed at.

explorerBlock.description: An interactive canvas widget — title bar, canvas, an accessible non-visual data-table fallback, 0+ sliders, 0+ live readout rows, an optional note. This is a REFERENCE + EXACT-SHELL block, not a generic reusable explorer type: canvasId/every control id/every readout id must match strings that public/js/engine.js's existing, per-explorer, hand-written JS already looks for — this schema does not invent new explorer behavior or let an author make up new ids. Its job is only to place the correct HTML shell (with those exact, pre-existing ids) at the right point in the chapter's reading order, and to hold the surrounding text bilingually. Verified against 3 real explorers (docs/DECISIONS/0003) — a genuinely different explorer shape (e.g. drag-based, multi-canvas) may need its own new block kind rather than being forced into this one.

title.description: The 'ex-top' title, e.g. '⊙ Explorer · Sharing in a ratio'.

canvasId.description: Exact id — must match what engine.js already wires up for this specific explorer.

ariaLabel.description: The canvas's aria-label — a real, load-bearing accessibility field, not decorative.

dataPanel.description: The 'View as data (non-visual equivalent)' accessible fallback — a real, deliberate accessibility feature (see project a11y-sweep history), not optional polish.

btnId.description: Exact id of the toggle button.

panelId.description: Exact id of the hidden panel — engine.js toggles its 'hidden' attribute.

descId.description:
Exact id of the

engine.js fills with a live description.

rowsId.description: Exact id of the <tbody> engine.js fills with live rows.

controls.description: Sliders. Empty/absent if the explorer has none.

valueDisplayId.description: Exact id of the <span> engine.js live-updates with the current value.

label.description: May contain simple inline HTML, e.g. 'Part a =' — matches source.

readouts.description: Live-updating readout rows below the controls. Empty/absent if the explorer has none.

id.description: Exact id of the <span class="v"> engine.js live-updates.

colorClass.description: Optional CSS color class on the row, e.g. 'indigo'/'amber' — matches source exactly, purely presentational.

note.description: Optional small note callout below the controls.

style.description: def=definition, thm=theorem/rule, note=informational, warn=practice problem or caution, pf=proof, example=worked example (renders in the site's <div class="example"> wrapper), example-card=a worked example rendered in the smaller <div class="fcard"> stat-card wrapper instead (a real, if less common, pattern — e.g. qudrat ch.6/ch.8's extra worked examples), tip=study-strategy tip. Maps to a template-owned CSS class — content authors pick a semantic style, not a class name.

label.description: Optional heading line, e.g. 'Definition — Antiderivative' or 'What to expect'. Many callouts have one; not all.

body.description: Main prose. LaTeX allowed (\( \) inline, \[ \] display).

copyLatex.description: Optional: if this callout has a 'Copy LaTeX' button (rare — 7 instances sitewide as of WP6), the LaTeX string it copies. Math notation, not translated.

subtitle.en: Quantitative reasoning for Qiyas's General Aptitude Test

body.en: The General Aptitude Test (GAT — القدرات العامة, "Qudrat") is administered by Qiyas. Alongside a verbal section it has a quantitative section that measures reasoning with numbers rather than memorised content.
body.ar: يُدار اختبار القدرات العامة (GAT) من قِبل المركز الوطني للقياس ("قياس"). إلى جانب القسم اللفظي، يضم الاختبار قسمًا كمّيًا يقيس التفكير المنطقي بالأرقام بدلاً من المحتوى المحفوظ.

body.en: Questions are multiple choice and are answered without a calculator, so speed and clean mental methods matter as much as the mathematics.
Estimate before computing; keep fractions instead of converting to decimals where possible.
A student answers 36 out of 45 questions correctly. What percentage is that? <details><summary>Show solution</summary>80%.</details>
